clusters.name: Caffeine Intoxication & Withdrawal
items: Intoxication (>250mg): Restlessness, Excitement, Flushed face, Diuresis, GI disturbance, Tachycardia (DSM p.569-570)
Withdrawal: Headache (hallmark), Fatigue/drowsiness, Dysphoric mood/irritability, Flu-like symptoms (DSM p.571-572)

clusters.name: Inhalant Intoxication
items: Incoordination, Slurred speech & Unsteady gait (DSM p.605)

criteria.thresholds: SUDs: >=2/10 criteria/12 mo (DSM p.587, p.590, p.601); Caffeine Intoxication: >=5/12 symptoms (>250mg) (DSM p.569); Caffeine Withdrawal: >=3/5 symptoms (DSM p.571); Inhalant Intoxication: >=2/13 symptoms (DSM p.605)
subtypes: Caffeine Use Disorder - Section III only (DSM p.910)

epidemiology.prevalence: Hallucinogen SUD: 0.2% adolescents (12-17), 0.4% young adults (DSM p.592); Inhalants: 2.3%-2.7% annual use in adolescents (DSM p.603; Dulcan p.223); Caffeine: >85% daily consumption (DSM p.569)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Hallucinogens: Male > Female (60% M in adults) (DSM p.593); Inhalants in adolescents: 1:1 equal (2.4% F vs 2.2% M) (DSM p.607); PCP: 62% M in treatment (DSM p.589)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Inhalants: Peak onset age 14 (DSM p.604); Hallucinogens: Peak age 18-25 (DSM p.592)
epidemiology.prognosis: Inhalant & Hallucinogen use typically remits in young adulthood; chronic inhalant use causes irreversible leukoencephalopathy (DSM p.604, p.712)

etiology.neurobiology: 5-HT2A receptor agonism on cortical pyramidal neurons (LSD/psilocybin) (StahlNeuro p.567); Open-channel NMDA block at PCP site -> GABA interneuron shutdown -> glutamate burst (PCP/ketamine) (StahlNeuro p.457, p.478); Adenosine A1/A2A antagonism restoring D2 sensitivity (caffeine) (StahlNeuro p.440); GABA-A/NMDA CNS depression + myelin dissolution & leukoencephalopathy (inhalants) (DSM p.603; StahlNeuro p.505)
etiology.environmental: Peer drug use, high income/urban setting for MDMA (DSM p.593); Poverty, homelessness, indigenous isolated communities for inhalants (DSM p.603-604)

first_line: Family-based therapy (MDFT, FFT, MST, A-CRA) for adolescent SUD (Dulcan p.236-239)
Quiet low-stimulation room + verbal 'talk down' for bad trips (Dulcan p.608)
Lorazepam (0.05 mg/kg) for acute agitation/panic (Dulcan p.608; StahlKids p.281)
second_line: Short-term atypical antipsychotics (Risperidone, Olanzapine) for acute hallucinogen psychosis (Dulcan p.608)
Clonidine for severe HPPD distress (DSM p.599; StahlNeuro p.567)
key_side_effects: Chlorpromazine contraindication in PCP (exacerbates anticholinergic burden/seizures) (Dulcan p.608)
Epinephrine contraindication in inhalant toxicity (triggers fatal arrhythmia) (DSM p.604; Dulcan p.221)
treatment.monitoring: ECG & respiratory monitoring in severe caffeine (>5-10g) or inhalant intoxication; urine toxicology (note inhalants negative) (DSM p.570, p.603; Dulcan p.231)

items: CRAFFT screener (6 items, >=2 positive indicates high risk) (Dulcan p.230)
S2BI (Screen to Brief Intervention) for AAP risk stratification (Dulcan p.229)
DSM-5 Level 1 Cross-Cutting Measure (Domain XI: any positive score requires Level 2 NIDA-ASSIST) (DSM p.846)
Standard urine drug screen is NEGATIVE for inhalants (DSM p.603)
key_numbers: 250 mg threshold for Caffeine Intoxication (DSM p.569)
8 days PCP detection window in urine (DSM p.589)

items: HPPD vs Hallucinogen Psychosis: Intact reality testing in HPPD (DSM p.599)
PCP vs Stimulants: Vertical/horizontal nystagmus & analgesia unique to PCP (DSM p.589, p.595)
Caffeine Intoxication vs Panic Disorder / Mania (DSM p.255, p.570)
Caffeine Withdrawal Headache vs Migraine: 25mg caffeine challenge test resolves headache in 30-60 min (DSM p.573)
anti-NMDAR Encephalitis mimicking PCP/ketamine dissociation (Dulcan p.608)
key_numbers: 25 mg caffeine challenge dose for withdrawal headache (DSM p.573)
30-60 minutes for headache relief post-caffeine (DSM p.573)
14 peak age for inhalant intoxication (DSM p.604)

high_yield: No withdrawal criterion exists in DSM-5-TR for classic hallucinogens, PCP, or inhalants (DSM p.546, p.588, p.591, p.603)
Intact reality testing is the essential prerequisite distinguishing HPPD from hallucinogen-induced psychosis (DSM p.599)
Vertical or horizontal nystagmus combined with analgesia is the pathognomonic diagnostic sign for PCP intoxication (DSM p.589, p.595)
Caffeine Use Disorder DOES NOT exist in DSM-5-TR Section II (Section III research criteria only) (DSM p.545, p.910)
Headache is the hallmark symptom of caffeine withdrawal occurring in 50% of cases (DSM p.572)
Standard urine drug screens cannot detect volatile inhalants; diagnosis is strictly clinical (DSM p.603; Dulcan p.231)
Inhalant use peaks at age 14 and is unique for equal sex prevalence in adolescents (DSM p.604, p.607)
Epinephrine is strictly contraindicated during inhalant resuscitation due to myocardial sensitization causing Sudden Sniffing Death (DSM p.604; Dulcan p.221)
5-HT2A receptor rapid downregulation mediates cross-tolerance across classic hallucinogens (StahlNeuro p.567)
PCP blocks NMDA receptors in open channels on GABA interneurons, causing cortical glutamate disinhibition (StahlNeuro p.457, p.478)
